question.text: A PM's NIFTY-100 portfolio has a realised beta of 1.1 over the last year. The CAPM expected return is computed as Rf=7%, Rm=14%. Using CAPM, what is the portfolio's expected return?

explanation.text: The Logic: CAPM: Re = Rf + β(Rm − Rf) = 7% + 1.1 × (14% − 7%) = 7% + 1.1 × 7% = 7% + 7.7% = 14.7%. The Trap: 15.4% uses β on Rm (wrong); 21.0% multiplies Rm; 13.7% drops Rf. Cross-Exam Context: Core CAPM; appears in XV Ch 12, X-A Ch 3, XXI-A. XXI-B expects fluency. Manager's Pro-Tip: CAPM's Rm assumption is the single most controversial input — use forward-looking ERP (5–6% for India) rather than historical in LRS-era forecasts.
